newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Feb 3.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp may have to cut part of its production for at least a week after a weekend fire at a brake parts plant of subsidiary Aisin Seiki Co Ltd. But other group companies are preparing to supply parts on behalf of Aisin. Brake parts supply will face the most serious shortages on Tuesday and Wednesday. Final decision on whether to suspend output will be made on Monday.

Trade Ministry and Ministry of Agriculture plan to reform the commodity futures market by cutting transaction fees to one-six of current levels -- about the same level as in Europe and the United States. They will also simplify listing requirements and procedures to allow listing of new items, including gasoline, crude oil and copper, within two to three years. Two ministries will target full implementation by 2001.

Sankyo Co Ltd plans start sales of a new diabetes medication that is effective in combating insulin resistance in Japan from early March. It plans to begin sales in the United states from March or April through a subsidiary it established in November. Sankyo obtained the development and marketing rights from Warner-Lambert Co, which recently obtained authorisation for the drug. It also plans to sell the drug in Europe by the end of this year.
